reviews.question:
With the rapid development of communication technology; e.g. smart phones, tablets and other mobile devices, some people believe that the disadvantages outweigh the advantages.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
Opinions are divided whether the drawbacks that the rapid development of brought is far more than benefits. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.
Admittedly, one might argue that the negative impacts caused by the rapid advancement by communication technology are greater than its advantages. This is predicated, initially, on the assumption that social network platforms, by nature, can make it relatively easy to fake identity. It naturally follows that users can be more vulnerable to cyber attacks, leading to the increasing number of reports of online scams using hacked social media accounts or stolen personal identification numbers. However, identity theft has always been a problem that is not primarily due to the lack of security of a particular networking site or application but rather due to users’ carelessness. Since that, with proper care and attention, social network users can protect themselves from fraud by adjusting privacy control settings and turning on two-step verification, which plays an important role in reducing the incidence of identity theft overall.
To add further credence to my assertion, I note the appreciable benefits of the rapid development of communicating by technology-devices. The chief advantage of this tendency is that long-distance communication facilitated can be enable people to connect no matter where they are. Furthermore, nowadays, individuals from all concerns of the globe can interact instantly through messaging or video calls although this case was rare in the past, when people had limited chances to engage with others outside their immediate surroundings. This can be clearly seen in the business sector, since virtual meetings and cross-border collaboration becomes the norm with video conferencing allowing participants from different time zones to join discussions, they can reduce travel costs and speed up decision-making. As a result, it can be particularly beneficial for startups and small businesses aiming to expand internationally. 
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that the advantages of the rapid development far outweigh its disadvantages.
reviews.overall: Em bám đúng hướng phản đối và giữ gần đủ chuỗi ý, gồm phần thừa nhận rủi ro rồi phản biện và ví dụ kinh doanh ở thân bài 2. Tuy nhiên, nhiều cụm ở mở bài và thân bài chưa có cấu trúc hoàn chỉnh nên người đọc khó hiểu ý chính. Em cần viết lại, trước hết sửa câu nêu quan điểm và các cụm thiếu chủ ngữ hoặc động từ, rồi soát lại từng câu phức trước khi nộp.

reviews.question:
Some people think that the increasing use of computers and mobile phones for communication has a negative effect on young people’s reading and writing skills.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
The increasing dependence on computers and mobile phones for communication has raised concerns about the development of young people’s reading and writing abilities. Some people believe that these devices have a negative impact on these skills. Personally, I am of the opinion that the disadvantages are more significant than the benefits.

The most noticeable effect can be seen in young people’s reading skills. Nowadays, they tend to read short and bite-sized pieces of information on social media instead of longer texts. As a result, they may find it difficult to stay focused for a long period of time, which can lead to problems with reading comprehension when they have to deal with books or academic materials. To make matters worse, frequent notifications from social media platforms can easily distract them while they are trying to read. Therefore, their ability to understand and concentrate on longer texts may be further affected.

Another negative impact is related to writing skills. Online communication is often characterised by the use of slang, abbreviations and emojis, and people do not always follow grammar and punctuation rules for the sake of convenience. In addition, young people increasingly rely on functions such as text prediction and autocorrection on computers and smartphones. This can make them less careful about spelling and grammar mistakes. Such informal language may be acceptable in daily conversations, but it is much less appropriate in formal contexts, such as academic essays, business proposals or professional correspondence.

In conclusion, although computers and mobile phones make communication more convenient, I believe that their increasing use can have a considerable negative effect on young people’s reading and writing skills.
reviews.overall: Em bám đúng hướng đồng ý và phát triển đủ cả reading lẫn writing skills theo dàn ý Cô giao. Đoạn reading có chuỗi nguyên nhân–kết quả rõ, đồng thời đoạn writing giữ đủ ngôn ngữ không trang trọng, cách dùng ngữ pháp/dấu câu và autocorrection. Em cũng dùng câu nêu quan điểm, paraphrase và từ nối tự nhiên. Khi tự viết bài sau, tiếp tục giữ cách giải thích từng bước rõ như bài này.

reviews.question:
The Internet has transformed the way information is shared and consumed, but it has also created problems that did not exist before.
What are the most serious problems associated with the Internet and what are the possible solutions?
reviews.originalEssay:
The rapid development of the Internet has completely changed the way people share and consume information. However, this technological progress has also brought about several problems that were not common in the past. In my view, cyberbullying and the manipulation of information are two of the most serious issues, and they should be dealt with through greater public awareness and appropriate regulations.

One of the chief problems associated with the Internet is cyberbullying. Social media platforms can be used to spread hurtful comments, rumours and false information to thousands of people in a very short time. The most serious point is that this type of bullying is difficult for victims to escape because the harmful content can continue to appear online even after they leave a particular platform. Another major issue is the lack of regulation over the information posted on the Internet. Malicious people can take advantage of this situation to spread misleading information or manipulate public opinion. For example, political campaigns can use targeted advertisements on social media to influence people’s decisions, which shows how powerful online information can be.

There are several possible solutions to these problems. First, awareness campaigns should be organised to educate people about the risks associated with using the Internet, especially cyberbullying. Celebrities and other public figures who are trusted by the public can help spread these messages through their social media platforms. For example, they can discuss the psychological distress that a bullied person may have to endure. Second, governments should introduce stricter regulations to control harmful content and misleading advertisements online. However, these regulations should be carefully designed because excessive control may affect freedom of speech.

In conclusion, cyberbullying and information manipulation are two major problems created by the Internet. Raising public awareness and introducing reasonable regulations can help reduce their negative effects while still protecting people’s freedom of expression.
reviews.overall: Em trả lời đủ hai phần của đề, bố cục rõ và phát triển tốt chuỗi bắt nạt trên mạng. Tuy nhiên, ở ý thao túng thông tin em đã thay ví dụ Cô giao bằng ví dụ chung về political campaigns. Phần giải pháp cũng cần nói rõ vì sao việc kiểm soát nội dung khó: chính việc quyết định nội dung nào là bất hợp pháp có thể mang tính chủ quan và hạn chế tự do ngôn luận. reviews.question:
The government should invest more money in teaching science than other subjects for a country’s development and progress.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
Some people argue that governments should invest more money in teaching science than in other subjects because science plays an important role in a country's development and progress. While I agree that science education deserves considerable financial support, I do not believe that it should always receive more funding than other academic subjects. The appropriate level of investment should depend on each country's specific circumstances.

On the one hand, in less technologically advanced countries, giving more funds to science-related subjects can bring significant benefits. Many developing nations need a stronger scientific workforce to improve their productivity and develop important economic sectors. With sufficient financial support, schools can build modern laboratories and organize regular scientific projects, which may motivate more students to become interested in science. In the long term, these students can become competent scientists, researchers and skilled workers in fields such as agriculture, manufacturing and healthcare. Therefore, investing more in science education can help these countries improve their technological capacity and support economic development.

On the other hand, in more developed countries, science and technology may already be relatively strong, so focusing too much on science education is not necessarily the best use of public money. These countries also have to deal with other important problems, such as social inequality, mental health and the loss of cultural identity. Subjects like history, literature and ethics can help students think more deeply, understand different cultures and appreciate their own traditions and customs. In addition, the arts can develop emotional understanding and creativity, which are also important for creating a balanced society. Other academic areas can even support scientific development. For example, ethics can help people consider how new technologies should be used in a fair and responsible way, while artistic thinking can provide scientists with new ways of looking at problems.

In conclusion, although science education is particularly important for countries that are less technologically developed, I believe governments should not automatically prioritize it over all other subjects. A balanced investment in science, humanities and the arts can help a country develop technologically while maintaining its culture, creativity and human connection.

reviews.question:
Many people argue that in order to improve educational quality, high school students should be encouraged to make comments or even criticism on their teachers. Others; however, think it will lead to loss of respect and discipline in the classroom.
Discuss both views and give your opinion.
reviews.originalEssay:
Many people argue that high school students should be encouraged to make comments or even criticize their teachers in order to improve the quality of education. Others, however, believe that this practice may result in a loss of respect and discipline in the classroom. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why I partly agree with the first opinion.

On the one hand, there are several reasons why students should be allowed to give feedback to their teachers. Firstly, comments from learners can give teachers more chances to understand their students’ learning needs. Based on these feedbacks, teachers can modify their teaching methods to make lessons more suitable and effective for their students. This can bring clear benefits to students’ academic progress. Secondly, regular evaluations from students can prevent teachers from becoming complacent. Knowing that their teaching methods will be evaluated may encourage them to continuously improve their teaching styles and methodologies, which can enhance the teaching and learning environment as a whole.

On the other hand, allowing students to criticize their teachers without any conditions can also cause some problems. Some students may assess their teachers based on their personal feelings and preferences rather than their teaching abilities. For example, a student might consider a teacher’s performance poor simply because he does not like the teacher’s appearance or fashion style. Furthermore, if every student is encouraged to make comments freely, there could be a large number of different opinions in the classroom. Since students have different expectations and learning preferences, it would be almost impossible for teachers to find a teaching method that satisfies everyone. As a result, this could create confusion and even reduce respect for teachers.

In conclusion, both views have their own valid points. Personally, I believe that students should be encouraged to give comments and criticism, provided that these evaluations are made in a constructive and objective manner. In this way, teachers can receive meaningful feedback while students can also benefit from a better learning environment.
reviews.overall: Em đã bàn đủ hai quan điểm và kết bài nghiêng về việc cho học sinh góp ý khi việc đánh giá mang tính xây dựng, khách quan. Hai đoạn thân bài giữ được cả hai lý do và các bước giải thích Cô giao. Em cần viết lại mở bài bằng cách diễn đạt của mình: hiện tại hai câu đầu gần như lặp đề, còn “partly agree” chưa nói rõ điều kiện em nêu ở kết bài. Cô cũng sửa “feedbacks” thành “feedback”; cách dùng số nhiều này có sẵn trong nguồn, nên Cô không tính là lỗi riêng của em.

reviews.question:
Schools are no longer necessary because children can get so much information available through the Internet, and they can study just as well at home.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
Some people argue that schools are no longer necessary because children can access a huge amount of information through the Internet and study just as effectively at home. Personally, I disagree with this view because although the Internet provides great support for education, schools still play an essential role in students’ academic and social development.

On the one hand, it is undeniable that the Internet has made educational content more accessible than ever before. Nowadays, children can easily find video tutorials, e-books and interactive learning tools on almost any subject, and many of these resources are free of charge. For self-motivated students, this flexibility can be a useful supplement to their studies, as they can learn at their own pace and choose materials that suit their needs. However, having access to a large amount of information does not mean that students know how to learn effectively. Young learners may lack discipline, critical thinking skills and time-management abilities to organise information independently. Without guidance from trained teachers, they may become overwhelmed by the amount of information online and even develop a superficial or incorrect understanding of a subject.

On the other hand, the role of schools goes far beyond simply providing academic knowledge. One of the main purposes of schools is to provide a structured learning environment where students can develop important life skills, such as teamwork, communication and discipline. Teachers can also explain difficult concepts, give feedback and help students identify their weaknesses, which is difficult to achieve when studying alone at home. Furthermore, schools are important social spaces where students can cooperate with others, face challenges and deal with different emotions. Through these real-life interactions, children can gradually become more confident and develop their social and emotional skills, which cannot be fully gained through studying online.

In conclusion, although the Internet offers students convenient access to a wide range of educational resources, I do not believe that it can completely replace schools. Traditional schools are still necessary because they provide not only academic instruction but also professional guidance and valuable opportunities for social and personal development.

reviews.question:
In today’s world of advanced science and technology, people still greatly value artists such as musicians, writers, and painters.
What can the arts tell us about life that science and technology cannot?
reviews.originalEssay:
With the development of technology and science, people nowadays still greatly value artists such as musicians, writers and painters. This essay will, accordingly, provide insight into what arts can tell us about life that science and technology cannot.
Arts excels in transmitting human emotions, which science and technology often fail to capture. For example, the response of our body and brain to nervousness and excitement can be exactly the same. This can be seen in the way our palms begin to sweat, how our heart starts to beat faster, and how adrenaline is produced in a certain region of the brain, which even the most advanced medical technologies such as MRI scanners, which could detail how our brain responds to external and internal cues and show identical results for those two feelings. However, science still cannot tell what a person is really going through while arts can deliver such unique emotions. To illustrate, a song which can express the joy of falling or the agony and heartbreak in a way that numbers and graphs cannot, as a result it is not surprising that there are now billions of songs about love, yet each tells a different story and a different shade of feelings.
Arts provides insights into abstract human problems that remain unsolved by science. For instance, questions such as “What is happiness?” still puzzle psychoanalysts, philosophers, and scientists alike. In scientific terms, happiness is explained as the presence of certain conditions, say, personal achievement, material possessions, or a stable relationship. However, real life proves otherwise, as many individuals with fame, wealth, and seemingly perfect families still suffer from deep misery, sometimes even leading to suicide. While science struggles to explain this paradox, writers, composers, and painters have long portrayed such inner pain through poems, songs and paintings. This can be seen in the fact that Billie Eilish, who is one of the most successful singers in the US vividly conveyed her loneliness beneath glamour and success in When the party is over.
In conclusion, I believe that despite the rapid development of technology and science, the ability of arts to convey emotions and abstract ideas cannot be replaced.
reviews.overall: Em đã trả lời đúng hai hướng của đề: nghệ thuật diễn tả cảm xúc riêng và những câu hỏi trừu tượng về đời sống. Em cũng đưa ví dụ phù hợp cho cả hai đoạn và dùng ngôn ngữ có mức độ như “often”. Tuy nhiên, mở bài gần như lặp lại đề mà chưa nêu trực tiếp hai câu trả lời. Ở Body 1, câu về máy MRI và câu về bài hát chưa hoàn chỉnh về cấu trúc, làm mạch so sánh khó theo dõi. Em hãy sửa hai câu này, thêm “in love” sau “falling”, rồi tự soát hòa hợp chủ ngữ–động từ.

reviews.question:
Some people think history has nothing or little to tell us, but others think that studying the past can help us better understand the present.
Discuss both views and give your opinion.
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that learning history is futile or has little advantage, while others believe that studying the past can help us better understand the present. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought.

Admittedly, one might argue that learning about the past cannot provide any useful information for learners since learning about historical events is merely a recording of facts from a bygone era, and such facts are only relevant to the specific contexts in which they occurred. Besides that, given the rapid advancement of science and technology, today’s world has evolved so much that lessons from the past might be irrelevant. For example, strategies used in ancient wars might no longer apply to contemporary attacks, which involve cyber-attacks, artificial intelligence and economic sanctions that did not exist on traditional battlefields. Furthermore, insights gained from history can appear disconnected from present-day realities.

However, I strongly believe that seemingly trivial and useless historical facts can provide invaluable lessons for today’s world. By studying the root causes of past wars, we can learn how to prevent conflicts and promote peace. In addition, while civilizations invading one another believed that they could only prosper at the expense of others, history shows that such a belief is false. Global cooperation is essential for national growth, and armed conflicts bring nothing but economic losses, which result not only from the cost of weapons but also from the decline in economic activity. This can also explain why many leaders strived for peace and political stability to ensure their nations’ prosperity and progress. Thanks to such insights, people can recognize the valuable benefits of studying the past.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although the lessons from history may be outdated for application in today’s world, they can still be beneficial in improving our societies.

Cô muốn em nối câu cuối Body 1 như một hệ quả của ví dụ, rồi đối chiếu rõ lợi ích hợp tác với thiệt hại do xung đột ở Body 2. reviews.question:
Most people have forgotten the meaning behind traditional or religious festivals; during festival periods, people nowadays only want to enjoy themselves.
To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that most people have forgotten the meaning behind traditional or religious festivals, and they only want to spend this time enjoying themselves. Personally, I am of the same school of thought.

On the one hand, the underlying meaning of festivals in many places has largely been forgotten. This can be clearly seen in the way Vietnamese people interpret the meaning of activities during Tet very differently, especially younger generations, who often think that giving money to children during this holiday is a token of good luck. However, this interpretation is far from the truth. According to tradition, giving money to children is a way to protect them from evil spirits, as the money acts as a bribe so that malevolent spirits do not harm the children.

On the other hand, religious and traditional festivals are becoming occasions for celebration. For instance, in Vietnam, Tet used to be a festival period when people spent time shopping, decorating their homes and enjoying traditional meals with their families. Conversely, most young Vietnamese people now look forward to Tet as an occasion to have fun during a long holiday period, rather than a time to engage in traditional activities. Besides that, many of them consider going to temples a way to pray for good fortune and asking for traditional calligraphy a fun activity rather than a religious one, while many others decide to go on a trip instead of spending time with their families.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that the deeper meanings of the cultural and religious values behind festivals are gradually being forgotten, as people increasingly view these occasions merely as opportunities to take a long break and enjoy themselves.
reviews.overall: Em đã trả lời cả hai vế của đề và triển khai đủ các ví dụ về Tết trong dàn ý. Cách nêu quan điểm 'I am of the same school of thought' rõ và đúng chức năng. Tuy vậy, câu mở bài vẫn lặp gần nguyên văn nhận định của đề; em cần diễn đạt lại bằng cấu trúc của mình. Hai Body cùng ủng hộ một quan điểm, nên cặp 'On the one hand / On the other hand' chưa thể hiện đúng quan hệ giữa chúng. Em sửa hai chỗ ấy và tách rõ ví dụ đi chùa, xin chữ.

First, the underlying meaning of festivals in many places has largely been forgotten. This can be seen in the way some Vietnamese people interpret activities during Tet. For example, younger generations often regard giving money to children as a gesture of good luck. This difference in interpretation suggests that the custom's older meaning may no longer be widely known.

Furthermore, religious and traditional festivals are increasingly treated as occasions for personal enjoyment. Although these customs can also be enjoyable, they keep families involved in the festival's traditions. By contrast, many young Vietnamese people now look forward to the long holiday primarily as an opportunity for fun rather than for traditional activities. Some focus on their own good fortune when visiting temples, while others treat asking for traditional calligraphy mainly as a fun activity. Many also choose to travel instead of spending time with their families. These examples show how personal enjoyment can become more prominent than the customs associated with the festival.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that the traditional meanings of festivals are gradually being forgotten in many places as people increasingly view these occasions as opportunities to take a break and enjoy themselves.
